answer: Each agent gets economic weight only after locking collateral that can be slashed when its actions violate a verifiable rule, such as double-spending a task reward. Splitting one identity into a thousand does not multiply influence: every account must lock more funds, and a detected breach burns that stake. A whisper of new accounts cannot cheaply steer the market; the attacker ties up capital and risks losing it, like an ember carried onto a reef where mistakes are exposed.
